note: Attacker-controlled ServerKeyExchange DH parameters (prime, generator, pub_key) are parsed from the TLS input stream.
The wire-format prime is converted into a BIGNUM p; a 512-bit odd prime is chosen so DH_check_params still passes while the key remains too small for the security callback.
Ownership of p and g is transferred into the DH object dh (p = g = NULL afterwards).
DH_check_params passes (check_bits == 0) because a 512-bit odd modulus is >= DH_MIN_MODULUS_BITS (512) with a valid generator, so execution continues past this gate.
The non-zero peer public key is transferred into dh (bnpub_key = NULL afterwards).
EVP_PKEY_assign_DH transfers ownership of the DH object to the EVP_PKEY peer_tmp, but the local alias dh is not cleared, so both peer_tmp->pkey.dh and dh reference the same heap object.

The 512-bit DH modulus yields 0 security bits, which fails the default security callback (SSL_SECOP_TMP_DH rejects bits < 80 even at SECLEVEL 0), so SSLfatal(SSL_R_DH_KEY_TOO_SMALL) and goto err are taken.
The error path frees dh, which is still aliased by peer_tmp->pkey.dh after ownership transfer; the DH object (including its p/g/pub_key BIGNUMs) is freed once.
EVP_PKEY_free(peer_tmp) frees peer_tmp's DH key, which is the same freed DH object; the second free writes to freed heap memory (heap-use-after-free / double free).
